title: `NormalModalLogic` lacks closure under uniform substitution, widening `BoxdotConjecture`
summary: `Arxiv.«1308.0994».NormalModalLogic` requires only `extK`, `mp` and `nec` and omits closure under uniform substitution, so `BoxdotConjecture` quantifies over necessitation-closed K-theories such as KT ∩ Th(M), which contains `□p₀ → p₀` but not `□p₁ → p₁`, whereas the source's conjecture is about normal modal logics, which are closed under substitution.

title: `polyToLaurent` maps t to X, not X⁻¹, so `huang_shi_theorem_1_2` quotients by SL₄(F[X])
summary: `Margulis.polyToLaurent` sends the polynomial generator to `HahnSeries.single 1 1`, embedding F[t] into F((X)) by t ↦ X, so `huang_shi_theorem_1_2` asserts relatively compact full diagonal orbits in SL₄(F((X)))/SL₄(F[X]), where none exist, whereas the source's theorem concerns SL₄(F((t⁻¹)))/SL₄(F[t]), which requires the generator to map to X⁻¹.

title: `phiSeq` excludes only denominators equal to an earlier term, not those dividing one
summary: `Erdos1000.phiSeq` drops a fraction only when its reduced denominator equals an earlier term `n j`, whereas the source excludes every fraction representable with an earlier denominator, that is whenever the reduced denominator divides `n j`, so the sequence overcounts and `phiAvg` and the theorem statements built on it count the wrong quantity.

title: `variants.erdos_hajnal` forbids induced bicliques where the source forbids ordinary ones
summary: `Erdos1036.erdos_1036.variants.erdos_hajnal` assumes `NoLargeInducedBipartite G (c * Real.log n)`, which rules out only induced copies of K_{a,b} in `G` and `Gᶜ` (parts independent or complete), whereas Erdős–Hajnal forbid every ordinary balanced biclique in `G` and `Gᶜ` with edges inside the parts unrestricted, so the Lean hypothesis is satisfied by graphs such as joins of Ramsey graphs that the source excludes.

title: `variants.max_non_convex_components` restricts the maximum to one component per root
summary: `Erdos1047.erdos_1047.variants.max_non_convex_components` takes the maximum number of non-convex components only over sublevel sets `sublevelSet f c` whose component count equals `(f.rootSet ℂ).ncard`, whereas Goodman's question ranges over all polynomial sublevel sets, and the restriction changes the answer already in degree 2, where `z² − 1` at level `9/8` has one connected non-convex component but is excluded.

title: `parts.ii` requires only a unit segment's endpoints to lie in `R`, not the open segment
summary: `Erdos1071.erdos_1071.parts.ii` admits a unit segment into the maximal family whenever its endpoints `seg.1` and `seg.2` lie in the open connected region `R`, so a segment passing through a point outside `R` is admitted and an open segment with endpoints on the boundary of `R` is excluded, whereas the source counts open unit intervals contained in `R`.

title: `variants.EHSNumbers_one_half` asserts density exactly 1/2, whereas the source conjectures density 1
summary: `Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half` states `EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2)`, that the density exists and equals exactly 1/2, whereas the source only remarks that finite data trend toward around 0.5 and then conjectures that the density exists and equals 1, so the variant states a claim incompatible with the source's prediction and omits the density-one conjecture.

title: `variants.upper_lower_d5_odd` upper bound has coefficient (p−1)/p, not (p−1)/(2p)
summary: `Erdos1085.erdos_1085.variants.upper_lower_d5_odd` bounds `f d n` above by `↑(d / 2 - 1) / ↑(d / 2) * n ^ 2 + c₂ * n ^ (4 / 3)`, whereas the source states the upper estimate with leading coefficient `↑(d / 2 - 1) / (2 * ↑(d / 2))` as in the lower conjunct, so for `d = 5` the Lean coefficient is 1/2 rather than 1/4 and the upper conjunct already follows from `f d n ≤ n.choose 2`.

title: `f` is eventually zero for every `r`; `f_asymptotic_2` and `_general` use little-o for `≫`
summary: `Erdos1092.f r m` fixes one subgraph size `m`, so for `m > r + 2` the complete graph `K_{r+2}` has no `m`-vertex subgraph and forces `f r m = 0`, whereas the source bounds the deleted edges at every subgraph size simultaneously, and `f_asymptotic_2` and `f_asymptotic_general` encode the source's linear lower bound `f_r(n) ≫ n` as `=o[atTop]`, which demands superlinear growth, instead of `=O[atTop]`.

title: `variants.granville_soundararajan` selects Wieferich primes, not non-Wieferich primes
summary: `Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan` concludes that the set of primes `p` with `2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]`, the Wieferich primes, is infinite, whereas the cited Granville–Soundararajan theorem asserts infinitely many non-Wieferich primes, those for which the congruence fails, so the conclusion lacks a negation and its docstring repeats the same error.

title: `variants.lower` and `variants.upper` assert unspecified constants, losing the leading 1 and 2
summary: `Erdos1104.erdos_1104.variants.lower` and `Erdos1104.erdos_1104.variants.upper` bound `triangleFreeMaxChromatic n` by `c₁ * sqrt(n / log n)` and `c₂ * sqrt(n / log n)` for some unspecified constants `c₁ ≤ 1` and `2 ≤ c₂`, whereas the cited results give the asymptotic leading constants `(1 - o(1))` and `(2 + o(1))`, so the Lean statements are strictly weaker corollaries.

title: `antiRamseyNum` counts colours on `s(v,v)` and forbids non-injective rainbow homomorphisms
summary: `SimpleGraph.antiRamseyNum`, used by `Erdos1105.erdos_1105.parts.i` and `parts.ii`, requires `Function.Surjective c` for a colouring `c` on `Sym2 (Fin n)`, so colours used only on the diagonal pairs `s(v,v)`, which are not edges of `K_n`, are counted, and it forbids every rainbow homomorphism `H →g ⊤` rather than only injective ones, whereas the source counts colours on edges and forbids rainbow copies of `H`.

title: `erdos_1110` requires coprimality with `p*q`, not pairwise coprime nonrepresentables
summary: `Erdos1110.erdos_1110` concludes that infinitely many non-representable `n` each satisfy `Nat.Coprime n (p * q)`, whereas the source asks for infinitely many mutually coprime nonrepresentables, an infinite family of non-representable integers that are pairwise coprime, a condition the Lean statement does not impose.

title: `variants.shelah_consistency` asserts the counterexample outright, not its consistency
summary: `Erdos1175.erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency` asks, via `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`, whether an ℵ₁-chromatic graph all of whose triangle-free subgraphs have chromatic number below ℵ₁ exists in the ambient universe, whereas Shelah's result states only that the existence of such a graph is consistent with ZFC.

title: `variants.schoen`, `variants.baier` hold for all large N, not just infinitely many
summary: `Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.schoen` and `Erdos12.erdos_12.variants.baier` conclude with `=O[atTop]`, asserting `|A ∩ [1,N]| ≤ C N^(2/3)` (respectively `C N^(2/3)/log N`) for every sufficiently large `N`, whereas Schoen's estimate and Baier's improvement hold only for infinitely many `N`, so both declarations state a strictly stronger eventual bound than the cited theorems.

title: `melfi_construction` holds trivially: exponent cutoff 0, no summability, bases 0 and 1
summary: `Erdos124.erdos124.melfi_construction` allows exponent 0 in `sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0`, so the representability condition holds for any `d`, bounds `∑' i, (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹` without `Summable`, so divergent series pass with `tsum = 0`, and requires only `StrictMono d` without `2 ≤ d 0`, so base 1 is allowed, whereas Melfi's theorem concerns bases at least 2, a convergent reciprocal series and positive exponents.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5540 (open pull request) adds `2 ≤ d 0` and `Summable (fun i ↦ (d i - 1 : ℝ)⁻¹)` to `melfi_construction`, covering the missing base bound and the unsummable `tsum`; the exponent cutoff `sumsOfDistinctPowers (d i) 0`, which makes representability automatic, is not addressed there.

Related: #5536 (open issue) reports the missing summability hypothesis and the missing `2 ≤ d 0` in `melfi_construction`; it does not raise the exponent-0 cutoff in `sumsOfDistinctPowers`, which trivializes the representation condition on its own.

title: `erdos_137` answer slot has the opposite polarity to the source's question
summary: `Erdos137.erdos_137` identifies `answer(sorry)` with the statement that no product of at least three consecutive positive integers is powerful, whereas the source asks whether such a powerful product exists, so `answer(True)` asserts a negative answer to the cited question and the docstring's "That is" sentence switches between the two opposite questions.

title: `erdos_142` and `variants.three` ask only for `=Θ[atTop]`, not an asymptotic formula
summary: `Erdos142.erdos_142` and `erdos_142.variants.three` relate `r k` to the answer by `=Θ[atTop]`, which fixes only the order of growth and is satisfied by `fun N => 2 * (r k N : ℝ)` as well as by `r k` itself, whereas the source asks for an asymptotic formula, a function whose ratio to `r k N` tends to `1`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4923 (open issue) is the tracking list 'Possible misformalizations II'; it mentions Erdős 142 only in passing, as a cross-reference to #4922 in its 'Existing tracking' section, and makes no claim about this file's statements.

Related: #4922 (open issue) concerns `erdos_142.variants.upper`, whose Big-O answer slot admits the trivial comparison function `N`; it does not address the `=Θ[atTop]` relation in `erdos_142` and `variants.three` above.

title: `variants.le_eleven_thirds` admits α = 11/3, but the cited 1997 result needs α < 11/3
summary: `Erdos145.erdos_145.variants.le_eleven_thirds` assumes `α ∈ Set.Icc 0 (11 / 3)`, admitting the endpoint α = 11/3, whereas the cited 1997 result establishes the moment asymptotic only for α < 11/3, so the declaration adds an endpoint the source does not cover.

title: `erdos_195` ranges over `ℤ ≃ ℤ`, doubly infinite arrangements instead of one-sided ones
summary: `Erdos195.erdos_195` takes the supremum over all `f : ℤ ≃ ℤ`, so it asks for the largest monotone arithmetic progression unavoidable in every doubly infinite arrangement of the integers, whereas the source poses the problem for one-sided arrangements `a₁, a₂, …` indexed by `ℕ` and treats the doubly infinite case as a separate question.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4896 (open issue) is a tracking issue whose entry for this file concerns the `answer(sorry) = sSup {...}` self-answer idiom; it does not address the indexing of the permutation by `ℤ` instead of `ℕ` described above.

title: `erdos_272` asks only for an asymptotic for `maxArithInterCard`, not the exact maximum
summary: `Erdos272.erdos_272` asks only for a function asymptotically equivalent to `maxArithInterCard` under `~[atTop]`, whereas the source asks for the largest cardinality for every `N ≥ 1`, so the answer `fun N => (N : ℝ)^2 / 2` satisfies the Lean statement while giving 1/2 at `N = 1`, where `maxArithInterCard 1 = 1`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5556 (open pull request) marks `erdos_272` research solved with answer `N^2/2`, proving the asymptotic from the Szabó variant, and keeps the `~[atTop]` headline, so it does not address the defect above.

title: `erdos_274` answer slot is the negation of the source's existence question
summary: `Erdos274.erdos_274` places `answer(sorry) ↔` before the assertion that every nontrivial exact covering of a nontrivial group has two parts of equal cardinality, whereas the source asks whether an exact covering with pairwise distinct coset sizes exists, so the right-hand side is the negation of the source question and `answer(True)` would encode the source's negative answer.

title: `greedyUnitFractionRem` reuses denominators; `variants.graham` quantifies outside answer
summary: `Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem` picks each next denominator from all of `A` without excluding those already used, so it can subtract the same unit fraction twice, whereas the source's greedy algorithm uses distinct denominators, and `erdos_282.variants.graham` places its quantifiers over `x`, `a`, `d` and their hypotheses outside `answer(sorry)`, so a fixed answer is asserted for each instance separately rather than for the universal question.

title: `erdos_283` and `variants.graham_alpha` range over `ℤ[X]`, not integer-valued polynomials
summary: `Erdos283.erdos_283` and `erdos_283.variants.graham_alpha`, together with the predicate `Condition` they use, quantify over `p : ℤ[X]`, polynomials with integer coefficients, whereas the source and Graham's conjecture concern integer-valued polynomials, so admissible polynomials such as `x(x−1)/2`, which is integer-valued with positive leading coefficient and no fixed divisor, are omitted.

title: `erdos_289` requires the intervals only to be disjoint, not separated
summary: `Erdos289.erdos_289` asks only that the `k` integer intervals be pairwise disjoint, so adjacent intervals such as `[2,3]` and `[4,5]` count separately, whereas the source requires `k` separated intervals with at least one integer between any two of them.

title: `variants.upper` admits negative intermediate iterated logs, forcing `R 13 < 0` when r = 4
summary: `Erdos321.erdos_321.variants.upper` requires only `1 ≤ Real.log^[2 * r] N`, which, since Mathlib's `Real.log x = log |x|`, permits intermediate iterates to be negative, so at N = 13 and r = 4 the hypotheses hold while the asserted upper bound on `R 13` is about -3.47, whereas the source's bound presupposes every iterated logarithm is positive.

title: `variants.wooley` uses exponent 0.917 in place of Wooley's 0.91709477
summary: `Erdos325.erdos_325.variants.wooley` bounds the quantity by `x ^ (0.917 : ℝ)`, whereas the cited Wooley result gives the exponent 0.91709477, so the declaration states a strictly weaker bound than the best-known one its docstring advertises, the two Big-O rates differing by the unbounded factor `x ^ 0.00009477`.

title: `erdos_326` fixes no order on the subbasis and rejects the zero limit the source allows
summary: `Erdos326.erdos_326` lets the subbasis `Set.range b` be an additive basis of any order via `IsAddBasis` and requires that `b n / n ^ 2` converge to no real limit, zero included, whereas the source asks whether some minimal asymptotic additive basis of order two has `a n / n ^ 2` tending to a nonzero limit.

title: `variants.example` liminf divides by 2 not `A n`; deletions range over values not indices
summary: `Erdos346.erdos_346.variants.example` requires `liminf (fun n => A (n + 1) / (2 : ℝ)) atTop = 1`, which equals 0 for every unbounded natural-valued `A`, whereas the source requires the lower limit of the consecutive ratios `A (n + 1) / A n` to be 1, and it models deletions as infinite sets of values `B ⊆ range A`, whereas the source deletes infinitely many terms of the sequence counted with multiplicity.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5571 (open pull request) changes the answer of the main theorem `erdos_346` to `False` and marks it solved, leaving its statement body and `variants.example` untouched, so it does not address the defects above.

title: `exists_t_for_k_disjoint_segments` accepts `k` pieces of one interval as `k` segments
summary: `Erdos349.exists_t_for_k_disjoint_segments` asks only for `k` pairwise disjoint intervals `I i` with `⋃ i, I i ⊆ {α | α > 0 ∧ IsGoodPair t α}`, which subdividing a single interval of good `α` supplies for every `k`, whereas the source asserts that the set of good `α` consists of `k` separate intervals, that is, has `k` connected components.

title: `variants.lower.white_2022` uses `<` where White's bound `μ ≥ 0.379005` is non-strict
summary: `Erdos36.minimum_overlap.variants.lower.white_2022` states the strict inequality `0.379005 < atTop.liminf MinOverlapQuotient`, whereas White's result is the non-strict bound μ ≥ 0.379005, so the Lean statement additionally rules out μ = 0.379005, which strict inequalities for every finite n do not justify after taking the liminf.

title: `erdos_363` asks finiteness of the union over all block counts and lengths, not fixed ones
summary: `Erdos363.erdos_363` applies `.Finite` to the set of all valid collections `S` with the number of blocks and the block lengths left free, so `answer(False)` asserts that the union over every parameter choice is infinite, whereas the source asks whether, for one fixed number of blocks with fixed lengths, there are infinitely many solutions.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5490 (pull request merged after the reviewed commit) adds `0 ∉ I` to `IsValidCollection` so that intervals containing 0 no longer make the statement trivially false; it leaves the quantifier structure of `erdos_363` unchanged and does not address the defect above.

title: `variants.three_two` asks for infinitely many pairs, not whether (8,9) is the only one
summary: `Erdos366.erdos_366.variants.three_two` asks whether the set of `n` with `(3).Full n` and `(2).Full (n + 1)` is infinite, whereas the cited source asks whether (8, 9) is the only such pair, a uniqueness question that a single further pair such as n = 12167 settles negatively without settling infinitude.

title: `variants.ae` requires convergence to `γ₀` on a cofinite set, not a density-one set
summary: `Erdos377.erdos_377.variants.ae` concludes with `∀ᶠ n in cofinite`, which by `Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop` states that `sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n` converges to `γ₀`, whereas the source states only that the sum equals `γ₀` up to a vanishing error on a set of `n` of density one, and ordinary convergence fails since infinitely many `n` have neither 3 nor 5 dividing the central binomial coefficient, giving a sum at least 8/15 > γ₀.

title: `erdos_40` asks whether some diverging function has the property, not which functions do
summary: `Erdos40.erdos_40` states the Prop that there exists a diverging `g : ℕ → ℝ` satisfying `Erdos40For g`, whereas the source asks to determine which diverging functions satisfy that property, so the declaration poses a yes/no existence question that leaves the set of admissible functions undetermined.

title: `parts.iii` assumes the density exists, and `variants.sigma` silently assumes termination
summary: `Erdos409.erdos_409.parts.iii` takes `hα : S_p.HasDensity α` as a hypothesis and concludes `α = answer(sorry)`, which every real answer satisfies when `S_p` has no density, whereas the source asks for the density itself, and `erdos_409.variants.sigma` asks for a natural-number `IsLeast` prime-hitting time, which exists only if the iteration terminates for every `n > 1`, while the source poses that count conditionally on termination.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4923 (open issue) flags, in its Erdős 409 entry, that the density `α` is a parameter of `parts.iii`, so `answer(α)` closes it by `rfl`, and proposes stating the density directly; the termination assumption in `variants.sigma` is not addressed there.

title: `variants.sigma`, `variants.density` demand a positive-density subset, not lower density
summary: `Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.sigma` and `Erdos418.erdos_418.variants.density` require, via `HasPosDensity`, a subset of the nonaliquot numbers (respectively the noncototients) whose natural density exists and is positive, whereas the cited sources state (respectively ask about) positive lower density, a strictly weaker condition since a set of positive lower density need not contain any subset of positive natural density.

title: `f` is a `partial def`, an opaque constant with no equation lemmas giving the recurrence
summary: `Erdos422.f` is a `partial def`, which Lean elaborates as an opaque constant `ℕ+ → ℕ+` with no equation lemmas, so the logic does not impose `f 2 = 1` or the recurrence `f n = f (n - f (n-1)) + f (n - f (n-2))`, whereas the source concerns Hofstadter's Q-sequence and the four statements in the file refer to a function with no logical specification identifying it.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4923 (open issue) lists self-answering statements across many files and notes that `growth_rate` here can be closed by `isBigO_refl`; it does not address the defect above, that `Erdos422.f` is a `partial def` with no equation lemmas tying it to Hofstadter's Q-sequence.

title: `erdos_429` quantifies the shift `n` over `ℕ`, so negative integer translates are never considered
summary: `Erdos429.erdos_429` ends with `∃ n : ℕ`, so `answer(False)` asserts only that some arbitrarily sparse admissible infinite `A` has no nonnegative shift `n` with `n + a` prime for all `a ∈ A`, whereas the source asks for an integer shift, and the admissible set `A = {p_k + 1}` with primes `p_k ≡ 1 mod (k+2)!` defeats every nonnegative shift while `A - 1` consists entirely of primes.

title: `greedy_sidon_construction` claims a Sidon subset of size ⌊√N⌋, not the greedy N^{1/3}
summary: `Erdos44.greedy_sidon_construction` asserts that for every `N ≥ 1` there is a Sidon subset `A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N` with `A.card ≥ N.sqrt`, whereas the cited greedy argument only yields a Sidon set of size at least N^{1/3}, and the greedy set up to 289 has 16 elements while `Nat.sqrt 289 = 17`.

title: `variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution` requires a density at every `z`, not a limit law
summary: `Erdos448.erdos_448.variants.hall_tenenbaum_distribution` requires the set `{n | tauPlus n / n.divisors.card ≤ z}` to have a natural density for every real `z`, whereas the cited Hall–Tenenbaum result is that `tauPlus n / n.divisors.card` has a limiting distribution, which yields convergence only at continuity points of the limiting CDF, so the Lean statement is strictly stronger.

title: `erdos_450` asks whether an `o(n)` scale suffices, not how large `y(ε,n)` must be
summary: `Erdos450.erdos_450` asks the yes/no question whether a sublinear scale `Y ε n` suffices, a question whose right-hand side is false because `localCount n n n = n − 1` exceeds `n / 2` for `n ≥ 3`, whereas the source asks how large `y(ε, n)` must be for the counting bound to hold and imposes no sublinearity.

title: `erdos_486` tests every modulus `n`, including `0` and `n ≥ m`, instead of `0 < n < m`
summary: `Erdos486.erdos_486` requires `(m : ZMod n) ∉ X n` for every modulus `n`, including `n = 0` (where `ZMod 0` is `ℤ`, so `X 0` alone can carve out an arbitrary set of `m`) and every `n ≥ m`, whereas the source only forbids residues modulo `n` for `0 < n < m`, so the stated set need not have a logarithmic density.

title: `variants.k_eq_3_card_gt_6` omits the exceptional cardinalities 27 and 486
summary: `Erdos494.erdos_494.variants.k_eq_3_card_gt_6` asserts `Erdos494Unique 3 card` for every `card > 6`, whereas the cited Selfridge–Straus result excepts the cardinalities 27 and 486, and the statement is false at 27: two distinct 27-element sets with identical multisets of triple sums exist.

title: `erdos_50_singular` demands singularity on all of ℝ though `f` is fixed only on [0,1]
summary: `Erdos50.erdos_50_singular` concludes `IsPurelySingular f`, which requires `f` to be continuous and singular on all of ℝ, whereas the hypothesis `IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f` constrains `f` only on `[0,1]`, so an admissible `f` made discontinuous at a point outside the interval satisfies the hypothesis and refutes the conclusion, while Schoenberg's theorem concerns singularity of the distribution on `[0,1]`.

title: `erdos_505` and its variants admit unbounded covering sets, whose `Metric.diam` is zero
summary: `Erdos505.erdos_505`, `erdos_505.small_dim` and `erdos_505.test_dim_one` require only `S ⊆ ⋃ i, F i` with `Metric.diam (F i) < Metric.diam S`, so taking every `F i = Set.univ` (unbounded, hence of real diameter zero) satisfies the covering conclusion, whereas Borsuk's problem concerns covers of `S` by bounded pieces of strictly smaller diameter, making `small_dim` and `test_dim_one` trivially true in every dimension and `erdos_505` false.

title: `KacCoefficients` uses Lebesgue measure, excluding every two-point uniform coefficient
summary: `Erdos522.KacCoefficients` takes `volume` as its default reference measure, and `erdos_522`, `zero_one`, `number_real_roots` and `yakir_solution` all use that default on the two-point sets `{-1, 1}` or `{0, 1}`, which have Lebesgue measure zero, so `h_unif` forces the law of each coefficient to be the zero measure rather than the fair Rademacher or Bernoulli distribution the source requires.

title: `erdos_538` asks whether `maxMass r N` has a limiting constant, not for the optimal bound
summary: `Erdos538.erdos_538` has a `Prop`-valued answer asking whether, for every `r ≥ 2`, `maxMass r N * log log N / log N` converges to some positive constant `c`, whereas the source asks to determine the best possible upper bound on the reciprocal mass, a question it does not pose as one of convergence and one that neither a negative answer nor the existential `c` settles.

title: `erdos_564` elaborates `c` as a natural, so `c * n` cannot express coefficients below 1
summary: `Erdos564.erdos_564` infers `c : ℕ`, so under `0 < c` its bound `2 ^ (2 ^ (c * n)) ≤ hypergraphRamsey 3 n` collapses to the fixed-exponent bound `2 ^ (2 ^ n) ≤ hypergraphRamsey 3 n`, whereas the source asks for some positive real `c`, possibly smaller than 1, in the exponent `2^(2^(cn))`.

title: `erdos_598` quantifies `m` outside `answer(sorry) ↔`, so the answer cannot be false
summary: `Erdos598.erdos_598` fixes the infinite type `m` outside `answer(sorry) ↔`, stating `∀ m [Infinite m], A ↔ P(m)` for the colouring-existence predicate `P`, whereas the source asks `A ↔ ∀ m [Infinite m], P(m)`; since `P(ℕ)` holds via a constant colouring, the template forces the answer to be true and `answer(False)` cannot express a negative answer.

title: `variants.he_ma_yang` uses the extremal-number threshold for all even q, not only q = 2^k
summary: `Erdos60.erdos_60.variants.he_ma_yang` requires the supersaturation bound above `extremalNumber (q^2 + q + 1) (cycleGraph 4)` for every even `q`, whereas He, Ma and Yang prove it above the explicit threshold q(q+1)^2/2 for large even q and above the extremal number only for q = 2^k, and since the extremal number falls below that threshold for infinitely many even q, the Lean statement asserts extra cases.

title: `erdos_672` answer has reversed polarity: its right-hand side asserts no example exists
summary: `Erdos672.erdos_672` places `answer(sorry)` opposite the statement that every admissible progression of `k ≥ 4` terms avoids every `l`-th power with `l > 1`, so `answer(True)` denies and `answer(False)` affirms the source's question, which asks whether the product of `k ≥ 4` consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression with coprime positive `n`, `d` can be a perfect power.

title: `variants.cambie_local_maxima` takes `ncard` of an infinite set, so it asserts `n^k ≤ 0`
summary: `Erdos692.erdos_692.variants.cambie_local_maxima` bounds `n^k` by the `ncard` of the set of `m` where `δ n` has a weak local maximum, but for every `n` and every valid density function that set is infinite (each `m = 36*s+28` with `s ≥ n` has `δ n (m-1) = δ n m = δ n (m+1)`), so the `ncard` is 0 and the statement asserts `n^k ≤ 0` eventually, whereas Cambie's result counts genuine local-maximum plateaus.

title: `erdos_70` and its variants colour `(𝔠).ord`, not the real line with its usual order
summary: `Erdos70.erdos_70`, `erdos_70.variants.erdos_rado` and `erdos_70.variants.omega_times_two_four` state the partition relation `OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 (𝔠).ord β n` on the initial ordinal of cardinality continuum, a well-order containing an ordered copy of `ω₁`, whereas the source and the cited Erdős–Rado theorem concern the real line with its usual order, which contains neither `ω₁` nor its reverse.

title: Summands may be 0 but `counting` starts at 1; `chen_fang` uses `counting A`, not the min
summary: `erdos_785`, `variants.ruzsa_lower_bound`, `variants.chen_fang_limsup` and `variants.chen_conjecture` let `A` and `B` contain 0 as a summand while `counting` counts only `A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x`, whereas the source takes both sets positive, so a shifted Ruzsa pair gives discrepancy tending to −∞; and `variants.chen_fang` bounds the discrepancy by a power of `counting A` with no hypothesis making `A` the sparse set, whereas Chen–Fang bound it by the smaller counting function.

title: `parts.i.selfridge` asserts density exactly 1/e − ε for a fixed set, not greater than it
summary: `Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.selfridge` concludes `A.HasDensity (1 / rexp 1 - ε)` for the set `A` fixed by the `let`, whereas Selfridge's construction gives `A` density greater than 1/e − ε, and since the same `A` cannot have two distinct densities for different ε the statement as written is false.

title: `A` is identically zero: `1 / 2` is natural-number division applied before the cast to ℝ
summary: `Erdos830.A x` is `0` for every real `x`, because `(1 / 2) * Finset.card` is formed in ℕ (where `1 / 2 = 0`) before the cast to ℝ, whereas the source defines `A(x)` as the number of amicable pairs up to `x`, so that `A(284) = 1`; hence the growth condition in `erdos_830.parts.ii` is unsatisfiable and the three `variants` are bounds on zero.

title: `erdos_855` lets the cutoff for y depend on x instead of requiring one uniform threshold
summary: `Erdos855.erdos_855` states `∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, ∃ Y, ∀ y ≥ Y, π (x+y) ≤ π x + π y`, so the threshold for `y` may depend on `x`, whereas the source asks for the inequality at all pairs with `x` and `y` jointly sufficiently large, that is a single `N` with `N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`.

title: `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` assumes only a Big-O bound for a single tuple
summary: `Erdos884.erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` quantifies `k` and `m` outside the implication and its hypothesis `HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m` is only an `IsBigO` upper bound, so it concludes `¬Erdos884Prop` from a bound on a single tuple (provable for `k = 0`, `m = fun _ => 1`), whereas Tao's result assumes the prime-tuples conjecture for every admissible tuple.

title: `variants.semiprimes` asserts only `M(n) ≫ g(n)`, losing the source's leading constant 1
summary: `Erdos888.erdos_888.variants.semiprimes` asserts only `M(n) ≫ g(n)`, where `M(n) = Nat.findGreatest (p n) n` and `g(n) = n * log (log n) / log n`, a lower bound with an unspecified positive constant that `g(n) / 2` also satisfies, whereas the cited semiprime result gives the sharp bound `(1 + o(1)) * g(n) ≤ M(n)` with leading constant `1`.

title: `variants.weisenberg` drops the Dickson's conjecture hypothesis of the cited conditional result
summary: `Erdos891.erdos_891.variants.weisenberg` asserts unconditionally, for every `k ≥ 2`, arbitrarily large intervals of length p₁⋯pₖ−1 whose elements all have at most `k` distinct prime factors, whereas the cited result establishes this only under Dickson's conjecture, which the theorem omits as a hypothesis.

title: `sawin_lattice_reduction` omits the size bound on `U.card`, leaving a density-only claim
summary: `Erdos90.sawin_lattice_reduction` concludes only that the unit-distance density of `U` exceeds a bound, with no upper bound on `U.card` and no shortest-vector parameter, whereas Sawin's Lemma 2 bounds the size of `U` by `(2R/ρ+1)^(2d)` at the same time as its unit-distance density, so the Lean conclusion holds for a suitable planar point set without any of the lattice hypotheses.

title: `variants.erdos_hajnal` asserts the `ℵ_ k` result unconditionally; the source assumes GCH
summary: `Erdos918.erdos_918.variants.erdos_hajnal` asserts, for every `0 < k`, a graph on exactly `ℵ_ k` vertices with chromatic number `ℵ₁` whose smaller induced subgraphs are countably colorable, whereas the cited result with these aleph cardinalities is proved under the generalized continuum hypothesis, and the paper's unconditional Theorem 2 uses successors of iterated powerset cardinalities instead of `ℵ_ k`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #4896 (open issue) tracks, for Erdős 918, a quantifier-scoping concern about a fixed `ω` versus a universal ordinal binder, and does not address the missing GCH hypothesis in `variants.erdos_hajnal` described above.

title: `variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5` uses exponent 1 - 2/(k+1) instead of 1 - 1/(k-1)
summary: `Erdos920.erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5` asserts a lower bound of the form n^(1 - 2/(k+1))/(log n)^c, which at k = 5 is n^(2/3)/(log n)^c, whereas the positive answer of Bradač it is presented as gives n^(1 - 1/(k-1))/(log n)^c, that is n^(3/4)/(log n)^c at k = 5, so the variant states a strictly weaker bound than the source.

title: `erdos_959` replaces the estimate of `extremalGap n` with a limit-existence question
summary: `Erdos959.erdos_959` states only that `log (extremalGap n) / log n` converges to some real number, whereas the source asks for a quantitative estimate of the order of `extremalGap n`, which the existence of a logarithmic exponent does not determine, since `n log n` and `n^(1 + c / log log n)` share exponent 1 while their ratio is unbounded.

title: `variants.generalization` negates `∀ k ≥ 2`, so a counterexample at one arity suffices
summary: `Erdos965.erdos_965.variants.generalization` places the quantifier over `k` inside the assertion negated by `answer(False) ↔`, so it states `∃ k ≥ 2, ¬ P(k)` with `P(k)` the positive `k`-sum assertion, a counterexample at a single arity that already follows from the `k = 2` theorem preceding it, whereas the cited result exhibits one colouring `f : ℝ → Fin 2` that is a counterexample for every `k ≥ 2`.

title: `variants.m2_bounds` asserts the bounds for every n ≥ 2 instead of sufficiently large n
summary: `Erdos973.erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds` asserts the lower and upper bounds on the greatest lower bound of max(‖a²+b²‖, ‖a³+b³‖) for every `n ≥ 2`, whereas the source states them only for all sufficiently large n, and the upper bound `1.745⁻²` already fails at `n = 2`, where that greatest lower bound is at least 2/5.

title: `ZhaoSolutionFree` admits nontrivial solutions; the conjectured lower bound is unsourced
summary: `Green16.ZhaoSolutionFree` forbids only solutions of `x + 2y + 3z = x' + 2y' + 3z'` with six pairwise distinct values, whereas the source forbids every nontrivial solution (one whose coefficients do not cancel within each equal-value class), so `Green16.g` and `Green16.zhao_question` concern the wrong avoidance condition, and `Green16.green_16_conjectured_lower_bound` asserts f(N) ≫ N exp(-c(log N)^(1/7)), which Green states only as an upper bound.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5005 (open issue) concerns the `answer(sorry)` slot of `green_16` sitting under the binder N, so that no closed answer can satisfy it; it does not address the defects above.

title: `green_41` and `variants.exists_better_bound` are met by the known Kravitz–Leng bound
summary: `Green41.green_41` and `Green41.green_41.variants.exists_better_bound` require only `minCopies ε < exp (exp (exp (ε ^ (-C))))` for some existentially quantified `C`, which the already-recorded Kravitz–Leng triple-exponential bound satisfies by enlarging the exponent, whereas the source asks for a genuine improvement on that bound (or, in Green's original question, for `minCopies ε` itself).

related_comments.comment: Related: #5553 (open pull request) proves `variants.exists_better_bound` with `answer(True)` from the Kravitz–Leng bound by enlarging the exponent `C` and marks it solved; the headline `green_41`, whose condition is met by the same bound, is left unchanged there.

Related: #5005 (open issue) concerns the `answer(sorry)` slot of `green_41` being scoped under `∀ ε` and suggests folding the headline into `exists_better_bound`; it does not address that the strict comparison with exp³(ε^(-C)) for an existential `C` is met by the known bound in either declaration.

title: Redirect to `erdos_689` gives only twofold coverage, not Green's tenfold question
summary: The file declares nothing of its own and points to `Erdos689.erdos_689`, whose coverage condition is `2 ≤ (...).card`, so it states the Erdős website's twofold question, whereas Green's problem 45 asks whether for all large `n` there are residues `a p` for the primes `p ≤ n` such that every `m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n` satisfies `a p ≡ m [MOD p]` for at least ten such primes.

title: `green_51.upper_ap` fixes the exponent at 2/3, dropping the ε in Ruzsa's bound 2/3 + ε
summary: `Green51.green_51.upper_ap` bounds `guaranteedMaxAPLength N α` by `exp (c * log N ^ (2/3))` for some constant `c` depending on `α`, whereas Ruzsa's cited result only gives `exp (c * log N ^ (2/3 + ε))` for every `ε > 0`, a strictly weaker bound since the fixed exponent cannot absorb the `ε` into the constant.

title: `green_54` and `green_54_known_case` dilate `K` by a scalar in place of Minkowski sums
summary: `Green54.green_54` requires `C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K` and `green_54_known_case` uses `C ⊆ (2 : ℝ) • K`, both scalar dilations `{r • x | x ∈ K}`, whereas the source takes the tenfold Minkowski sum `K + ⋯ + K` and the known case concerns `K + K`, sets that differ from the dilations because `K` is balanced but not assumed convex.

title: `NoKInLine` asserts exact saturation for all k > 2 and N ≥ k, which the sources leave open
summary: `Green72.NoKInLine` asserts `AllowedSetSize k N = (k - 1) * N` for every k > 2 and N ≥ k, whereas Green asks whether such saturation eventually fails and GK2025 leaves the maximum undetermined outside its large-k range, and this blanket assertion implies a negative answer to the question posed in `green_72`.

title: `kourovka_1_74` asks for one topologized Tarski monster, not all Platonov-minimal groups
summary: `Kourovka.«1.74».kourovka_1_74` asks only whether some Tarski monster admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology, whereas Problem 1.74 asks to describe all Platonov-minimal topological groups, those non-discrete Hausdorff groups whose proper closed subgroups are all discrete, a class that is not exhausted by Tarski monsters (the additive real line belongs to it) and that no declaration in the file characterizes.

title: `IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE` holds vacuously when the denominator `q` vanishes at `pt`
summary: `LamLitt.IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE` requires only that `q` be a nonzero polynomial and takes regularity from `IsDefined` with an unrelated numerator-denominator pair, so the cleared equation holds trivially when `aeval pt q = 0`, admitting `X` as a solution of `f′ = 0` and making `variants.integrality_implies_algebraicity` false for the non-algebraic series Σ binom(2k,k)² zᵏ/16ᵏ, whereas the source's ODE has a denominator nonzero along the solution.

title: `variants.weak_kahn_kalai` omits μ_t(F) = 1/2 and hard-codes the optimality constant 1000
summary: `Mathoverflow10799.mathoverflow_10799.variants.weak_kahn_kalai` quantifies over arbitrary intervals and lets the existential `C` scale only the interval length `C * n^ε` while `IsOptimal` keeps its fixed coefficient 1000, whereas the paper's weaker theorem requires the interval to end at the critical probability, where `μFamily t F = 1/2`, and makes the optimality coefficient itself depend on `ε`.

title: `conjecture` demands every large exponent lack a valid base, not just some exponent
summary: `OeisA103662.conjecture` states `∃ N, ∀ n > N, a n = 0`, that every sufficiently large exponent `n` has no base `b` with `IsValidZerolessPower n b`, whereas OEIS A103662 conjectures only that some exponent has no valid base, that is `∃ n, a n = 0`, a strictly weaker claim.

title: `conjecture` reverses the yes/no polarity: `answer(True)` denies any further zero
summary: `OeisA109905.conjecture` makes `answer(True)` equivalent to the set of positive indices `n` with `a n = 0` being exactly `{1, 6, 30, 54}`, that is, to the non-existence of any further zero, whereas the source asks whether another zero exists, so the Lean right-hand side is the negation of the source's proposition and the two answers are swapped.

title: `conjecture` holds when no prime pair `2^n ± m` exists, since `a` falls back to 0
summary: `OeisA113213.conjecture` bounds `a n`, which `a` sets to `0` via `s.headD 0` whenever no `m` with `(2^n - m).Prime ∧ (2^n + m).Prime` exists, so the big-O statement is equivalent to "no prime pair exists or some witness satisfies `m ≤ C * n^3`", whereas the source asserts that a prime pair with a bounded witness exists for all large `n`.

title: `kthPrimeFactor` indexes prime factors with multiplicity, not distinct prime divisors
summary: `OeisA382590.kthPrimeFactor` reads the k-th entry of `Nat.primeFactorsList` with repetitions, so `kthPrimeFactor 2 (a 6) = 2` and `kthPrimeFactor_periodic` concerns an eventually constant sequence, whereas the source's k-th prime factor is the k-th smallest distinct prime divisor, giving 5 at `a 6 = 20` and 7 at `a 7 = 896`.

title: `odd_of_isA038552` asserts radicand parity, not the odd-vs-even discriminant comparison
summary: `OeisA38552.odd_of_isA038552` states that for even `n` the largest squarefree radicand `k` with `IsA038552 n k` is odd, whereas the OEIS comment says the largest odd fundamental discriminant magnitude with class number `n` exceeds every even one, and these differ because a radicand `r ≡ 1 (mod 4)` such as 5 has even discriminant `-4r` and even radicands give magnitude `4r`, not `r`.

title: `conjecture1` ranges over all n unguarded, asserting infinitely many prime pairs p, 2p-1
summary: `OeisA46969.conjecture1` quantifies over every index `n` although `a005382` is defined via `Nat.nth` and returns 0 once the terms run out, so with finitely many primes `p` having `2 * p - 1` prime the conclusion would become `Nat.Prime 0`, making the statement assert infinitely many such primes, whereas the OEIS comment only claims `a p / 12` is prime for each such `p > 3`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5588 (open pull request) restates `conjecture2` as the negation of the universal claim, which fails at n = 236791, and marks it solved; it leaves `conjecture1` untouched and does not address the defect above.

title: `conjecture` assumes `(p n).Prime` rather than asserting the required prime exists
summary: `OeisA55487.conjecture` takes `hp : (p n).Prime` as a hypothesis and concludes only `a n = p n * q n`, so an index `n` where no prime meets the search conditions imposes no requirement, whereas Hasler's conjecture asserts for every non-factorial-prime `n ≥ 1` both that such a prime pair exists and that `a n` equals its product.

title: `SatisfiesBenford` states only the first-digit law, not the full significand distribution
summary: `OeisA87455.SatisfiesBenford` demands only the nine limiting frequencies of the leading digits `1` to `9`, whereas the cited source defines Benford's law by the limiting distribution of the whole significand, equivalently of all finite leading-digit blocks, a strictly stronger condition, so `OeisA87455.conjecture` asks only the first-digit version of the cited question.

title: `C1a` sups over `Icc (1/2) 1`, and the real Bochner integral and `sSup` force `C1a = 0`
summary: `Constant1a.C1a` takes the inner supremum over `Icc (1/2) 1` instead of the source's [-1/2, 1/2], and its real-valued Bochner convolution integral and real `sSup` both return 0 on nonintegrable or unbounded values, so `f ≡ 1` forces every admissible `C` to be nonpositive and the definition evaluates to `C1a = 0` rather than the source's autocorrelation constant.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5559 (open pull request) changes the inner supremum's range in `C1a` from `Icc (1/2) 1` to `Icc (-1/2) (1/2)`, fixing the interval defect; the Bochner integral returning 0 for nonintegrable convolutions and the real `sSup` returning 0 for unbounded convolution values are not addressed there.

title: `reachability_decidable` fixes `d` outside `ComputablePred`, requiring no uniform decider
summary: `BranchingVAS.reachability_decidable` states `∀ {d : ℕ}, ComputablePred ...`, so it only asserts that each fixed-dimensional reachability predicate has some decider, with no requirement that these deciders depend effectively on `d`, whereas the source's decision problem asks for a single algorithm taking a branching vector addition system of arbitrary dimension together with a target as input.

title: `HasGδSingletons.lindelof_card` quantifies over all topological spaces, not Tychonoff ones
summary: `CardinalityLindelof.HasGδSingletons.lindelof_card` asks for any topological space `X` with `HasGδSingletons X`, `LindelofSpace X` and `𝔠 < #X`, with no separation hypothesis, whereas the cited paper asks for a Tychonoff (`T35Space`) Lindelöf space with points Gδ of cardinality greater than the continuum, so a non-Tychonoff witness satisfies the Lean statement without answering the source's question.

title: `countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable`: ω-monolithic, not monolithic
summary: `Homogeneous.countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable` assumes only `CountablyMonolithicSpace X`, that closures of countable subsets are metrizable, whereas Problem 17 in the source asks about monolithic compact spaces, where the closure of every subset of infinite cardinality κ has weight at most κ, so the Lean statement asks a stronger question under a weaker hypothesis.

title: `irrational_algebraic_normal_in_some_base` asks only for simple normality, not normality
summary: `AlgebraicNormality.irrational_algebraic_normal_in_some_base` concludes `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase b x`, a predicate that only requires each digit `d < b` to have limiting frequency `1/b` (simple normality, satisfied by `1/3` in base 2), whereas the source asks whether every irrational algebraic real is normal in some base, meaning every finite digit block of length `k` occurs with frequency `1/b^k`.

title: `conditional_artin_primitive_roots` assumes Dirichlet GRH, not RH for `ℚ(ζₖ, a^(1/k))`
summary: `ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.conditional_artin_primitive_roots.parts.i`, `parts.ii`, `variants.part_ii_power_squarefreePart_not_modeq_one` and `variants.part_ii_power_squarefreePart_modeq_one` assume `type_of% GRH.generalized_riemann_hypothesis`, the Riemann hypothesis for primitive Dirichlet L-functions over `ℚ`, whereas Hooley's conditional theorems assume the Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta functions of the fields `ℚ(ζₖ, a^(1/k))` for squarefree `k`, which include nonabelian extensions such as `ℚ(ζ₃, 2^(1/3))`.

title: `all_fermat_squarefree` reverses the answer: asks if all Fermat numbers are squarefree
summary: `Fermat.all_fermat_squarefree` states `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, Squarefree n.fermatNumber`, whereas Wikipedia asks whether a non-squarefree Fermat number exists, so an affirmative answer to the Lean statement corresponds to a negative answer to the source's question and vice versa.

title: `variants.dim_3_or_higher` asserts failure in some dimension ≥ 3, not in every dimension
summary: `Fuglede.FugledeConjecture.variants.dim_3_or_higher` states `answer(False) ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n → FugledeConjectureFor n`, which is equivalent to `∃ n, 3 ≤ n ∧ ¬ FugledeConjectureFor n` and is proved by a counterexample in one dimension alone, whereas the source states that Fuglede's conjecture fails in every dimension `n ≥ 3`.

title: `exists_inscribed_rectangle_of_smooth`, `exists_inscribed_square_of_C2` admit cusps
summary: `InscribedSquare.exists_inscribed_rectangle_of_smooth` and `InscribedSquare.exists_inscribed_square_of_C2` require only `IsEmbedding γ` together with `ContMDiff` smoothness of `γ`, which allows a noninjective differential such as the cusp `γ(z) = (Re z, (Im z)^3)`, whereas the sources concern regular smooth and C² Jordan curves with nonvanishing velocity, so both theorems quantify over singular curves outside the cited results.

title: `variants.complex_function_field` omits the algebraically closed hypothesis on `K`
summary: `InverseGalois.inverse_galois_problem.variants.complex_function_field` asserts that every finite group is realizable over `RatFunc K` for any field `K` of characteristic zero, whereas the cited solved result requires `K` to be algebraically closed, so with `K := ℚ` the declaration claims every finite group is a Galois group over `ℚ(t)`, which via Hilbert irreducibility would settle the inverse Galois problem itself.

title: `variants.not_reciprocal` lacks irreducibility and `variants.odd` lacks nonreciprocity
summary: `lehmer_mahler_measure_problem.variants.not_reciprocal` bounds the Mahler measure of every integer polynomial with `f.reverse ≠ f` below by that of `X^3 - X - 1`, but the source restricts to irreducible polynomials and `X * lehmerPolynomial` passes the test with measure 1.176…, and `variants.odd` bounds every polynomial with odd coefficients by the golden ratio, whereas the source requires nonreciprocity and the reciprocal `X^6+X^5-X^4-X^3-X^2+X+1` has measure 1.556….

title: reversed implication in `variants.consequence`, and a strict `<` where the FLP theorem gives `≤`
summary: `mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence` states the converse of the cited implication, making the non-existence of Z-numbers the hypothesis rather than the conclusion of the oscillation bound, and `variants.flatto_lagarias_pollington` requires `1/p < Ω(p/q)` where the Flatto–Lagarias–Pollington theorem gives only `1/p ≤ Ω(p/q)`.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5524 (open pull request) reverses the implication in `variants.consequence`; the strict inequality in `flatto_lagarias_pollington` is not addressed there.

title: `…_of_real_roots` and `…_of_roots_same_norm` restrict roots of `p`, not of `p(X+z)-p(z)`
summary: `MeanValueProblem.mean_value_problem_of_real_roots` and `mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm` place the real-root and equal-norm hypotheses on the roots of `p` while concluding at every `z`, whereas Tischler's special cases place them on the nonzero roots of the normalized polynomial `p(X+z)-p(z)`, so `X^3 - X` meets the first hypothesis yet violates Tischler's condition at `z = 2i`, and fails the second hypothesis at `z = 0` although its nonzero roots `±1` have equal norm.

title: `HasNoetherProperty` ranges over all finite automorphism groups, not those permuting the indeterminates
summary: `NoetherProblem.HasNoetherProperty` quantifies over every finite subgroup of `L ≃ₐ[K] L` rather than the groups permuting the indeterminates, so `noether_problem` and its variants `two`, `three`, `four` and `forty_seven` state a strictly stronger claim than Noether's problem, one that is false in three and four variables.

title: `pi_normal_base_ten` asserts only simple normality: `IsNormalInBase` ignores digit blocks
summary: `NormalNumber.pi_normal_base_ten` uses `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase`, which only requires each single digit `d < 10` to appear with limiting frequency `1/10`, so the theorem asserts simple normality of π in base 10, whereas the source conjectures normality, in which every block of digits of every length ℓ has limiting frequency `1/10^ℓ`.

title: `isRegularPrime_iff_Bernoulli` includes odd Bernoulli indices, so every p ≥ 7 is irregular
summary: `RegularPrimes.isRegularPrime_iff_Bernoulli` requires `¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ (bernoulli' k).num` for every `k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (p - 3)`, including odd `k` such as `k = 3` where `bernoulli' 3 = 0`, whereas the source defines a regular prime by non-divisibility of the numerators of the even-indexed Bernoulli numbers B₂, B₄, …, Bₚ₋₃ only, so the stated condition fails for every prime p ≥ 7.

title: `variants.le_nine` admits degree 9, but the cited low-degree result stops at degree 8
summary: `Sendov.sendov_conjecture.variants.le_nine` assumes `hn : n ∈ Set.Icc 2 9` with `f.natDegree = n`, so it asserts Sendov's conjecture for polynomials of degree 2 through 9, whereas the cited low-degree result of Brown and Xiang establishes it only for degree n < 9, that is degrees 2 through 8, and the docstring repeats the same upper bound.

related_comments.comment: Related: #5560 (open pull request) marks `sendov_conjecture` as solved with a formal proof link and adds references, leaving `variants.le_nine` unchanged, so it does not address the degree bound above.

title: `IsSpider234` admits trees with a fourth leaf and a second branching vertex
summary: `SidorenkoConjecture.IsSpider234` requires only a tree with a degree-3 centre and leaves at distances `2`, `3` and `4` from it, a condition met by a ten-vertex tree with four leaves and two degree-3 vertices, whereas the source's (2,3,4)-spider has exactly three leaves and a single branching vertex, so `tournament_anti_sidorenko_spider234` also ranges over trees outside its cited case.

title: `snake_upper_bound` drops the `- 7` from the denominator, stating a stronger bound
summary: `SnakeInBox.snake_upper_bound` bounds the snake length by an expression whose denominator is `6 * n + (1 / (6 * √6) * √n)`, whereas the cited bound's denominator is `6 * n + (1 / (6 * √6) * √n) - 7`, so for every `n ≥ 2` the Lean right-hand side is strictly smaller (7129/217 versus 7087/175 at `n = 6`) and the declaration asserts a strictly stronger upper bound.

title: `IsTaxicabFor'` is vacuous at `n = 1` and `IsTaxicabFor` demands disjoint representations
summary: `Taxicab.IsTaxicabFor'` places the representation conditions inside the implication `L ≠ M → …`, so with `n = 1` the witness `S = {[]}` makes `IsTaxicabFor' k m 1 x` hold for every `x` and `IsTaxicabFor 3 2 1 0` holds, and `Taxicab.IsTaxicabFor` requires pairwise-disjoint lists rather than distinct unordered representations, so 5 = 1+1+3 = 1+2+2 is rejected and `IsTaxicabFor 1 3 2 6` holds instead.

title: `transcendental_catalanConstant_or_gompertzConstant` uses Catalan's constant where the source has Euler–Mascheroni
summary: `Transcendental.transcendental_catalanConstant_or_gompertzConstant` states that `catalanConstant` or `gompertzConstant` is transcendental over `ℚ`, whereas the cited result is that at least one of the Euler–Mascheroni constant `Real.eulerMascheroniConstant` and the Gompertz constant is transcendental, so the declaration asserts a different, unproved disjunction about Catalan's constant G = β(2).

title: `conjecture133` floors `l G` before comparing with `path G`, weakening the source bound
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture133.conjecture133` concludes `rad + ⌊l G⌋ ^ cC4 ≤ path G` for a C₄-free graph, whereas the source states `rad + l G ≤ path G` with no floor, and since `rad` and `path G` are integers the two bounds differ by one whenever `l G` is not an integer, as for `P₃` where `l = 4/3`.

title: `conjecture23` averages vertex-to-`M` distances, not pairwise distances within `M`
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture23.conjecture23` uses `distavg G M`, the average over all vertices `v` of the distance from `v` to the set `M`, whereas the source averages the distances between distinct vertices both belonging to `M`, and the two inequalities differ: on an 11-vertex spine with four attached triangles and pendant leaves the source's inequality fails while the Lean one holds.

title: `conjecture32` averages vertex-to-`A` distances, not the distances between members of `A`
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture32.conjecture32` uses `distavg G A`, defined as `(1 / |V|) * ∑ v, min_{a ∈ A} d(v, a)`, the average distance from all vertices to `A`, whereas the source averages the nonzero distances between members of `A`, so on the source's counterexample `P₅` with `A = {0, 4}` the Lean inequality `32/15 ≤ 5` holds while the source's `16/3 ≤ 5` fails.

title: `conjecture34` averages nearest-set minima including zeros, not nonzero pair distances
summary: `WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34.conjecture34` bounds the path number by `SimpleGraph.distavg G S`, the mean over all vertices `v` of the minimum distance from `v` to the set `S` (center or maximum-degree set), including the zero terms for `v ∈ S`, whereas the source averages all nonzero pairwise distances `d(s,v)` with `s ∈ S` and `v ∈ V`, that is the double distance sum divided by `|S|(|V|−1)`.
